key_patterns.name: Heterogeneous baseline risk perception
key_patterns.description: Agents exhibit diverse risk_perception values in [0,1], likely non-uniform and segmentable by age_group and occupation.
key_patterns.relevance: Maps to heterogeneous initial mask propensity and differential sensitivity to social influence; informs priors and stratified calibration.

key_patterns.name: Multiplex network structure
key_patterns.description: Three layers (family, work_school, community) with different tie densities and strengths; edges may be directed and overlapping across layers.
key_patterns.relevance: Layer-specific influence strengths and contact frequencies should be calibrated; directionality influences exposure asymmetry.

key_patterns.name: Clustered households and meso-scale work/school clusters
key_patterns.description: Family ties form small, dense cliques; work/school ties form medium-size clusters; community ties provide sparse bridging.
key_patterns.relevance: Expect faster local convergence within families, medium diffusion in work/school, and broader reach via community; guides weight and transmission parameters.

key_patterns.name: Early adoption driven by information exposure
key_patterns.description: train_data.csv includes received_info; adoption likely follows information receipt with a lag.
key_patterns.relevance: Estimate info-to-adoption hazard; separate exogenous information effects from peer influence to reduce confounding in calibration.

key_patterns.name: Potential homophily by age and occupation
key_patterns.description: Higher tie probability among agents sharing age_group or occupation; similar traits cluster in the network.
key_patterns.relevance: Adjust peer influence by similarity; homophily affects diffusion speed and critical thresholds.

key_patterns.name: Non-reciprocal edges in raw data
key_patterns.description: Adjacency lists may not be reciprocal; directedness can bias influence counts.
key_patterns.relevance: Requires symmetrization or explicit modeling of directed influence to avoid under/over-estimation of exposure.

key_patterns.name: Temporal convergence in late period
key_patterns.description: Adoption rates may stabilize toward the end of the calibration window (assess via decreasing day-over-day changes).
key_patterns.relevance: Use StabilityLastWindow to check convergence; helps tune persistence/decay parameters.

key_relationships.relationship: Information receipt increases next-day adoption probability.
key_relationships.strength: Estimate discrete-time hazard difference or average treatment effect; expect medium to strong.

key_relationships.strength: Estimate logistic slope lambda; strength varies by layer; family strongest.

key_relationships.relationship: Age segment differences in adoption propensity and responsiveness.
key_relationships.strength: Estimate group fixed effects; expect moderate heterogeneity.

key_relationships.strength: Estimate group effects and interaction with work_school layer exposure.

symmetrize_edges.source: Multiplex network JSON (edges may be non-reciprocal)
symmetrize_edges.notes: Use undirected edges by default; keep optional directed mode for sensitivity.

layer_weights.source: Multiplex network JSON degree/clustering contrasts and typical contact intensity
layer_weights.notes: Calibrate via grid/CMA-ES against RMSE; constrain to sum to 1.

contact_rate_per_day.notes: Alternative: normalize to 1 using layer_weights if modeling influence by fractions rather than counts.

self_loops_removed.notes: Drop any self-references in adjacency lists.

value.form: logit(P0_i) = alpha0 + alpha_risk * risk_perception_i + alpha_age[age_group_i] + alpha_occ[occupation_i]

initial_mask_prob_model.source: agents CSV (risk_perception, age_group, occupation) + day 0/early days in train_data.csv
initial_mask_prob_model.notes: Fit coefficients via logistic regression on earliest days with variation; replace priors above after estimation.

risk_perception_distribution.notes: Use as prior for agents missing risk_perception or for synthetic agents.

info_transmission_prob.notes: Estimate by regressing received_info_t on neighbors’ received_info_{t-1} per layer.

exogenous_broadcast_rate.source: train_data.csv received_info not explained by neighbors

peer_effect_strength_lambda.source: Calibration to adoption response vs neighbor adoption share
peer_effect_strength_lambda.notes: In logistic: logit(p_adopt) += lambda * I_i,t where I is weighted neighbor fraction.

conformity_threshold_theta.source: Threshold model fit to adoption curves
conformity_threshold_theta.notes: If using threshold rule: adopt when I_i,t >= theta (with noise).

homophily_multiplier.notes: Multiply influence weight when attributes match; calibrate via segment-specific fit.

adoption_rule.value: P(wear_t=1 | wear_{t-1}=0) = 1 - exp(-lambda_peer * I_i,t - beta_info * received_info_{t-1} - beta0)
adoption_rule.notes: beta_info estimated from info→adoption hazard; beta0 is baseline adoption rate.

persistence_phi.notes: Can be conditioned on exposure to model habit reinforcement.

dropout_base_delta.source: P(wear_t=0 | wear_{t-1}=1, low exposure) from train_data.csv
dropout_base_delta.notes: Allow exposure-dependent dropout: delta_t = delta0 * (1 - I_i,t).

target_adoption_threshold.notes: Adjust per policy goals; compute first day simulated adoption >= threshold.

stability_window_N.notes: Average absolute day-over-day change over last 7 days.

calibration_strategy.calibration_approach: Use a two-stage hybrid method: (1) Estimate micro-transition parameters from data via GLMs/survival models: initial propensity (alpha parameters), info→adoption effect (beta_info), persistence/dropout (phi, delta), and preliminary peer effect (lambda) using layer-weighted neighbor exposure. (2) Refine network-layer parameters and interaction strengths with simulation-based optimization (e.g., CMA-ES or Bayesian optimization) to minimize RMSE and MAE between simulated and observed daily adoption rates; include penalties for mismatch in PeakAdoptionDay, FinalAdoptionRate, and StabilityLastWindow. Apply stratified fits by age_group/occupation if segment residuals are systematic.
calibration_strategy.validation_strategy: Evaluate on held-out days and subgroups. Compute RMSE and MAE on daily adoption rates; report FinalAdoptionRate, PeakAdoptionDay, TimeToTargetAdoption (with threshold from parameters), and StabilityLastWindow (N=7). Perform posterior predictive checks: distribution of time-to-adoption, segment-specific adoption curves, and sensitivity to symmetrization. Use bootstrapping over agents to quantify uncertainty and provide confidence intervals.

file_summaries:
- Overall structure/type: Tabular CSV; each row represents a single agent. No nested structures.
- Primary key: agent_id (integer) — unique identifier for each agent; use as node ID in the social network and to join with other datasets (e.g., edges).
- Attributes:
  - age_group (categorical: e.g., Youth, Young Adult, Middle Age) — demographic segment that can inform homophily, contact patterns, and differential influence rules.
  - occupation (categorical: e.g., Student, White Collar, Blue Collar) — role for assigning agents to interaction layers (school, workplace) and contact rates.
  - risk_perception (float in [0,1]) — baseline perceived risk; suitable as initial mask-wearing propensity or as a parameter modulating susceptibility to social influence and responsiveness to external information.
- Relationships/nesting: None encoded in this file; no edges or households. Relationships are implied via attributes (e.g., same occupation → likely co-layer contacts) and should be constructed externally using agent_id.
- Use in simulation:
  - Instantiate agents with heterogeneous traits; agent_id indexes nodes.
  - Initialize behavior: map risk_perception to initial probability of mask-wearing (e.g., direct or via a logistic transform possibly conditioned on age_group/occupation).
  - Network construction: use age_group/occupation to form layers and homophilous ties; set contact frequencies and influence weights accordingly.
  - Dynamics: risk_perception can act as a stable trait or an updateable state influenced by neighbors and interventions; age/occupation can modulate thresholds, conformity, or exposure.
  - Analysis/interventions: segment outcomes and policies by age_group/occupation; target high-contact or low-perception segments.

- Overall data structure and type:
  - JSON object representing a multiplex (multi-layer) social network as adjacency lists.
  - Top-level is a dictionary keyed by agent IDs (strings), values are dictionaries of lists.

- Meaning of keys or columns:
  - Top-level keys ("0", "1", …): unique agent identifiers (convertible to integers).
  - Nested keys:
    - family: list of agent IDs connected via household/family ties.
    - work_school: list of agent IDs connected via workplace/school ties.
    - community: list of agent IDs connected via broader community ties.
  - List elements are neighbor agent IDs (integers) referencing other agents in the same file.

- Relationships or nested elements:
  - Each agent has up to three adjacency lists, one per social layer.
  - Edges are specified per agent; reciprocity is not guaranteed by the data (i.e., may be directed unless symmetrized during preprocessing).
  - Layers are disjoint categories but neighbors can overlap across layers (an agent can be connected to the same person in multiple layers).
  - No weights or timestamps are provided; this is purely topological structure.

- How this data should inform simulation entities or interactions:
  - Agents: create one agent per top-level key with ID and membership in three layer-specific networks.
  - Network construction: build three graphs (family, work/school, community) or a single multiplex graph with layer tags. Decide whether to:
    - Treat edges as directed (as given) or
    - Symmetrize to undirected by adding reverse links.
  - Interaction dynamics:
    - Use layer-specific contact frequencies/weights (e.g., family > work/school > community) to modulate influence of mask adoption.
    - At each step, an agent samples neighbors from each layer according to layer weights to compute social influence toward adoption/abandonment.
    - Support heterogeneous exposure by aggregating influences across layers (e.g., weighted sum or threshold rules).
  - Initialization and validation:
    - Ensure all referenced IDs exist; handle any missing nodes or duplicates.
    - Optionally compute degrees per layer to set behavior parameters (e.g., higher conformity in dense family clusters).
  - Extensions:
    - Allow cross-layer spillover effects, targeted interventions on specific layers (e.g., workplace mandates), and time-varying edge activation probabilities per layer.

Semantic metadata summary for train_data.csv:

- Data structure and type
  - CSV, long-format panel (time-series) data.
  - One record per agent per day; discrete-time steps.

- Columns and meanings
  - day: integer time index (non-negative), simulation timestep.
  - agent_id: integer unique identifier for an agent.
  - wearing_mask: boolean state indicating if the agent is currently wearing a mask.
  - received_info: boolean state indicating if the agent has received information/prompts about mask-wearing (e.g., via social contact or broadcast).

- Relationships or nested elements
  - No nesting; flat table.
  - Composite key (day, agent_id) identifies a unique state observation.
  - Temporal relationship: records for the same agent across increasing day values form a trajectory.
  - Potential causal/temporal dependency: wearing_mask at day t may depend on received_info and neighbors’ states at t-1 (network not included in this file).

- How this data should inform simulation entities or interactions
  - Agent initialization: use day 0 rows to set initial states for each agent (in sample, all agents start with wearing_mask=false and received_info=false).
  - State variables per agent: maintain booleans for wearing_mask and received_info; update each timestep.
  - Transition modeling/calibration: if multiple days exist in the full file, use it to estimate parameters (e.g., probability of adopting a mask after receiving info, persistence/decay, lag effects).
  - Validation/fitness: compare simulated trajectories to observed rows per (day, agent_id) to tune diffusion and compliance parameters.
  - Network dependency: social ties are not present here; must be provided/assumed elsewhere. received_info can be driven by network contagion or exogenous broadcasts; wearing_mask can depend on received_info and social influence.
  - Data handling: cast booleans correctly, treat day as discrete timestep, ensure full coverage or handle missing agent-days.
